application_review: Finite event majorization and a two-event union bound are proved for the original finite masses. Original raw rough harmonic interval probabilities are bounded using the retained sharp periodic harmonic discrepancy and original normalizer lower bound; the same unit density is canceled without an extra modulus loss.

The original pivot probability of lying below C*X or above X^2/C is at most 2*(log C+W/X)/(log X-W/X), whenever 1<C<=X and the original harmonic normalizer is positive by its proved sufficient condition. Support restrictions are proved explicitly, with real half-open interval endpoints.

For every tail product in [tlo,C*tlo], explicit endpoint inequalities ensure the entire pivot preimage is contained in the buffered cutoff. If some other tail product violates containment, the actual sample in that bin must lie below 2*C*X or above X^2/(2*C), provided 6*R<=X and C,X>=1.

The cutoff discard event allows any short bin containing the actual product sample and any witness tail product in the common range. Its original raw harmonic probability has the uniform bound 2*(log(2*C)+W/X)/(log X-W/X), independent of the positive dyadic lower product. The probability tends to zero when X tends to infinity, W/X and R/X tend to zero, and widths are nonnegative.

The zero-discard limit is instantiated for actual master cutoffs and primorial roughness moduli, including stage-dependent finite pivot choices. The required cutoff growth and ratios are derived from retained master growth theorems. Any width bounded by the pivot gap works, in particular M*(Nat.sqrt H/M), with its integer bound proved explicitly.

Reviewed interval normalization: the comparison interval may extend beyond the original cutoff, so only a proved upper bound is asserted. Original roughness is preserved in the interval mass, and its totient density cancels against the original positive normalizer lower bound.

Reviewed endpoint events: lower-band support restriction includes the lower endpoint, and the upper band includes equality at X^2/C while the original cutoff remains open at X^2. The union bound permits overlap and does not assume disjoint bands.

Reviewed discard geometry: the witness tail product can differ from the actual sample tail product. The proof checks the entire interval [tlo,C*tlo], including buffered cutoff margins 2*R. The fixed-factor enlargement requires 6*R<=X, proved eventually in the limit application.

Reviewed uniformity: the finite discard upper bound is independent of tlo, Q, the bin partition and sampled tail product. The existential discarded-bin event therefore contains every concrete bad-bin selection. The current theorem is for original raw pivot probability, not yet the full conditional exposure law.

Reviewed actual-scale specialization: cutoff divergence for a varying pivot follows by finite uniform choice, while primorial/X and R/X vanish by retained master gap bounds. The aligned natural square-root width bound is proved for all moduli, even zero; equivalence with the paper real-floor expression and its positive growth are not silently asserted.
All named declarations are strictly elaborated and checked for transitive axioms. Prior sources and prior axiom sets remain unchanged. No independent kernel replay or full-target proof is claimed.

StrongConjecture and the original full finite monochromatic sums/products claim remain unproved. Finite-list native periodic interval inverse existence remains an explicit unproved hypothesis; its genuine existence proof and positive uniform correlation constants must be supplied. Conditional Prediction includes actual admissible parameters, positive finite scale-list closure, common native unit observables and complete fixed-ultrafilter calibration and count limits. Conditional Alignment includes the canonical finite-word schedule, actual execution, positive palette-scale budgets, common positive denominator and certified actual auxiliary visits. Integer realization now proves the actual master pair scale relation, exact natural numerator with its original rational value, canonical bounded full-modulus residues, all required divisibilities, uniform eventual fixed-integer divisibility, finite numerical slot bounds and the numerical own-target array-letter identity. The actual earlier-variable exposure fixes every residue and slot shift, full own-target numerators and array residues; exact affine tail dependence of each progression and the whole own-target progression sum is proved. Concrete integer-input polynomial array groups, their common nilpotence bound, input translations, pointwise lattice coset evaluation and exact affine model linear orbits are constructed. The genuine original native Lie polynomial-array coefficient algebra, bracket closure, high-degree cutoff and finite dimension are now proved; literal Lie evaluation homomorphisms and their lower-central compatibility are constructed. The same-step lower-central cutoff of the genuine array Lie algebra, injectivity of all integer evaluations and simultaneous coefficient recovery by one fixed finite integer evaluation set are now proved, including for the original native model. The actual binary product native Lie algebra, componentwise original exponential and global logarithm, and integration and inherited topology of every product Lie subalgebra are now proved. The complete native array coefficient algebra now embeds by one fixed finite family of integer inputs into the native Lie algebra of an actual finite original-group product. Its finite evaluation image integrates to a closed contractible simply connected subgroup, uniquely parameterized by coefficient exponentials. All-integer multiplication compatibility, the exact full exponential array subgroup, its group isomorphism and inherited-topology homeomorphism with the finite image, contractibility, simply connectedness, and discreteness of its pointwise Gamma-valued subgroup for discrete Gamma are now proved. Cocompactness of the exact all-integer pointwise lattice is now proved by actual lattice monomial spanning, rational-log intersection, positive-root character descent and continuous quotient transfer. The actual integrated subalgebra and full native array group now have constructed smooth manifold and Lie group structures on their inherited topologies, and all literal integer evaluations are smooth. The actual array group and exact lattice instantiate the existing NativeNilmanifoldData interface at the same original nilpotency step, with constructed compatible quotient metric. Integer input translations now preserve the actual graded coefficient Lie algebra, the full native exponential array group and its exact all-integer lattice; actual group and coset homeomorphisms and continuous coset evaluation with exact translation compatibility are proved. Array input translations are now proved smooth with smooth inverses in the existing original exponential charts. Original affine power-times-basepoint model arrays are proved to belong to the actual native array group; their exact evaluations, input translations and linear time orbit are proved both in the group and in its exact lattice coset space. Actual original and array discrete-lattice quotient manifolds are now constructed on the retained coset topologies; original quotient projections, all integer-input quotient evaluations and original quotient translations are smooth, with the latter having proved smooth inverses. The dependent product joint group, its exact product lattice, compact coset space, common nilpotency cutoff, original joint model orbit, component evaluations and input shifts are now constructed with exact formulas. The finite joint group now has its constructed finite-dimensional complete Lie model, global product exponential diffeomorphism and original smooth group operations, and instantiates NativeNilmanifoldData with the exact joint group, exact lattice and same common step. The original joint quotient is a smooth manifold with smooth component integer evaluations and smooth input-shift diffeomorphisms. Uniform quantitative smooth-observable bounds and model-reading calibration remain unproved. The finite short-bin pivot likelihood estimate and factor-three posterior domination relative to the original tail prior are now proved for the actual raw harmonic pivot law, with explicit full-cutoff containment, positive normalizer, unit residue and small-discretization hypotheses. The original dyadic-conditioned tail law is now proved equal to conditioning the original product law, and is dominated by 2^card(T) times product uniform. The actual short-bin posterior is now dominated by 3*2^card(T) times product uniform on prescribed dyadic residue bins, with explicit endpoint inequalities ensuring every pivot preimage lies in the cutoff. The original raw pivot probability of discarding short bins whose full preimages leave the buffered cutoff now has a uniform explicit bound and is proved to tend to zero for the actual master cutoffs and primorial roughness moduli. The proof covers any width bounded by the pivot gap, including modulus-aligned integer square-root widths, and any positive dyadic lower product. The complete earlier-variable exposure disintegration, transfer of the cutoff-discard estimate through all prior good conditioning, treatment of cutoff-clipped dyadic bins, H-boundary bin probabilities, exact real-floor microcell identification and full microcell growth, and eventual satisfaction of the remaining scale inequalities are still to be connected. HasAlignmentMonomialRecurrence remains an explicit unproved input. Its genuine nilpotent recurrence proof, the connection of the constructed joint model to all prescribed quantitative readings, microcell boundary and point-law estimates, and positive-probability Alignment bounds remain unproved. Final ordered positive rapidly separated monochromatic extraction is incomplete. No unavoidable blocker is established. A complete public proof repository, official contribution PR, independent review and prize application remain pending; no completed prize submission is claimed.
